title: What If Character Were a Skill You Could Develop?
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article reframes character away from the common view of it as a fixed, innate essence and toward the idea that it can be built like a skill. It observes that which character traits society prizes shifts over time, citing humility's recent rise relative to the charisma and boldness once favored, as evidence that our standards for character are not fixed either. Drawing on how educators try to teach character to children, the piece argues that qualities like open-mindedness, self-control, and empathy can be codified, practiced, and strengthened through repetition. It closes with a direct challenge to readers to pick a character trait they admire and design a practice routine for developing it, then teach the approach to others. The archivist finds this one of the more reflective, developmentally oriented pieces in the newsletter's catalog.
points: The article challenges the common assumption that character is fixed and instead frames it as learnable.
Which character traits society values has shifted over time, from charisma and boldness to today's emphasis on humility.
Educators' efforts to teach character to children suggest traits like empathy and self-control can be practiced like skills.
The piece proposes treating any admired character quality as something to design deliberate practice around.
Readers are challenged to pick a trait, build a practice for it, and then teach the approach to others.
quotes: Common wisdom convinces us that cultivating a strong character is a pathway to a meaningful and productive life.
Character is judged against a specific set of values important to society at the time.
Our view of character, it seems, evolves as society places more or less emphasis on certain values, such as results or relationships.
But what if character was more fluid and malleable than many people believe? What if character is really a skill?
Skills such as open-mindedness, cooperation, reliability, self-control, and empathy can all be codified and performed.
Open your eyes to the possibility that character is a set of skills that can be amplified through practice.
